    Over-representation analysis of gene sets

    Source: R/bio-omics.R
    bio_enrich.Rd

    Tests whether a list of selected features (for example significant genes) contains more members of each gene set or pathway than expected by chance, using the one-sided hypergeometric test (Fisher's exact test for over-representation). Only features in the universe are counted. P-values are adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg method.

    Usage

    bio_enrich(
  .data,
  feature,
  selected,
  gene_sets,
  universe = NULL,
  min_size = 5,
  max_size = 500
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per feature, such as the output of bio_diff_expr(). All of its features form the universe unless universe is given.

    feature

    <tidy-select> The feature identifier column.

    selected

    <data-masking> A logical expression choosing the features of interest, for example p_adj < 0.05 & log2fc > 1.

    gene_sets

    Either a named list of character vectors or a data frame with columns gene_set and feature.

    universe

    Optional character vector of background features.

    min_size, max_size

    Gene sets with fewer or more members in the universe are skipped.

    Value

    A <bio_omics> sorted by p-value with columns gene_set, set_size, overlap, expected, fold_enrichment, p_value, p_adj and overlap_features (a list column).

    References

    Boyle, E. I. et al. (2004). GO::TermFinder: open source software for accessing Gene Ontology information and finding significantly enriched Gene Ontology terms associated with a list of genes. Bioinformatics, 20, 3710-3715. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bth456

    Examples

    de <- bio_diff_expr(expression_sim, gene, sample, count, condition,
  treatment = "stress", reference = "control", transform = "log2_cpm"
)
bio_enrich(de, feature, p_adj < 0.05 & log2fc > 0, gene_sets_sim)
